ez_redis_planning_prompt.mission:
EZ-Redis: Product Architecture and Implementation Planning
```
Build EZ-Redis, a production-grade developer tool that helps developers understand, design, optimize, and maintain Redis usage throughout their applications.
The long-term goal is to make EZ-Redis a natural part of the software development workflow, comparable in convenience and usefulness to Git. The product must help developers make better technical decisions, reduce Redis-related defects, improve caching performance, and simplify development without introducing unnecessary friction.
EZ-Redis must be more than an MCP server or an LLM wrapper. It should be a reusable Redis analysis and optimization platform consisting of a deterministic core engine, an intelligent decision layer powered by Jev, standardized integrations through MCP, and an optional autonomous agent built with LangGraph.
Prioritize correctness, measurable performance improvements, developer trust, minimal disruption, maintainability, and practical usefulness over architectural complexity.
Inspect the existing repository, conduct the necessary technical research, consult available specialist agents, critically evaluate the proposed architecture, and produce a comprehensive implementation plan.
Do not implement any feature or begin any implementation phase until I explicitly approve the completed plan.
```

ez_redis_planning_prompt.product_architecture:
Evaluate the proposed architecture, challenge its weaknesses, and improve it where supported by technical evidence. Treat the following components as proposed responsibilities rather than a requirement to implement every component.
```
EZ-Redis Core Engine
The core engine is the foundation of EZ-Redis and the source of truth for deterministic static analysis findings.
It must operate independently of an LLM, Jev, MCP, and LangGraph. Developers should be able to use core functionality through a Python API and CLI without requiring an AI provider or network access, except for operations that explicitly depend on external services.
Python JavaScript TypeScript TSX Java
Discover source files and identify supported languages. Parse source code and validate syntax where appropriate. Perform language-specific semantic analysis. Normalize relevant information into a shared Redis intermediate representation (IR). Perform control-flow, data-flow, and cache-key dependency analysis. Evaluate deterministic static-analysis rules. Correlate findings with runtime telemetry when available. Produce structured findings with source locations, evidence, severity, and limitations. Generate and evaluate optimization recommendations. Support optional repair, regression testing, and verification workflows.
Evaluate how the shared IR should represent:
Redis clients and client operations.
Commands, keys, values, and key construction.
TTL settings and expiration behavior.
Redis data structures and access patterns.
Read and write paths.
Cache invalidation and refresh mechanisms.
Transactions, pipelines, and scripts.
Relationships between cached values and authoritative data stores.
Cross-file dependencies and relevant program flows.
Evidence provenance, analysis confidence, approximations, and unknown information.
Evaluate support for dynamically constructed keys, aliases, cross-file references, wrappers, abstractions, decorators, framework integrations, and indirect Redis access.
Clearly distinguish syntax-level observations from resolved semantic relationships and inferred behavior. Syntax parsing alone must never be presented as proof of complete program semantics.
Design language adapters that can evolve independently while producing a common IR. Justify any language-specific capabilities that cannot be represented reliably in the shared model.
Analyze actual application caching behavior rather than relying exclusively on generic Redis best practices.
Missing, excessive, or inappropriate TTLs. Cache invalidation defects and stale-data risks. Inconsistent cache-aside implementations. Inefficient Redis commands and data structures. Excessive serialization and payload sizes. Cache stampedes and hot-key risks. Unnecessary cache misses and repeated database reads. Memory inefficiencies and eviction risks. Incorrect or inefficient rate-limiting implementations. Redis Search and vector-search usage. Connection management, transactions, pipelines, and batching. Application-level bottlenecks involving Redis. Key naming, expiration, data layout, and access-pattern optimization.
Classify each finding according to whether it can be established using static analysis, runtime evidence, or a combination of both.
For runtime analysis, investigate safe, opt-in integrations with Redis metrics, application telemetry, tracing, and controlled benchmarks.
Never claim that an optimization improves performance merely because a heuristic, LLM, or Jev predicts an improvement. Where practical, validate changes using representative measurements and disclose benchmark limitations.
Live Redis inspection must be read-only by default.
Operations that can modify data, change configuration, disrupt service, or affect production traffic require explicit authorization, appropriate isolation, and safeguards.
Do not assume all environments permit the same diagnostic commands or telemetry access.
Jev Decision and Recommendation Layer
Investigate current Jev documentation, supported APIs, integration mechanisms, capabilities, limitations, licensing, pricing where relevant, and service requirements.
Verify the current API and integration model rather than relying on assumptions or invented interfaces.
Jev should evaluate structured evidence about a repository and help EZ-Redis determine which caching patterns and optimization strategies best fit specific application data flows.
This is a central product capability, not merely a classifier that assigns severity to lint warnings.
Cache-aside. Read-through caching. Write-through caching. Write-behind caching. Prefetching and pre-populated caches. Other suitable Redis caching patterns or combinations of patterns.
Read/write ratios and access patterns. Authoritative data sources. Data freshness and consistency requirements. Cache invalidation and refresh behavior. TTL policies. Latency and availability requirements. Workload characteristics and runtime metrics. Failure behavior and operational complexity. Memory constraints and expected data volume. Existing application architecture and Redis usage.
The core engine extracts structured repository evidence. Candidate caching patterns are identified. Jev evaluates bounded, relevant decisions using the available evidence. Deterministic application logic applies compatibility constraints and decision policies. EZ-Redis generates a recommendation with supporting evidence, rationale, uncertainty, trade-offs, alternatives, and required follow-up. The developer reviews and approves or rejects recommendations before consequential changes occur.
Distinguish verified repository facts from assumptions, inferences, and missing information.
When requirements cannot be established from source code or telemetry, ask targeted questions instead of inventing requirements.
Evaluate how Jev should handle:
Missing or contradictory evidence.
Uncertain or ambiguous decisions.
Invalid or incomplete responses.
Unavailable external services.
Cases where no candidate pattern satisfies known constraints.
A Jev confidence score must not substitute for measured performance or correctness verification.
Jev must be isolated behind an internal interface. The core engine must remain independent of Jev's implementation, with deterministic fallback behavior when the service is unavailable or a reliable recommendation cannot be established.
LangGraph Coding and Optimization Agent
Evaluate LangGraph as an orchestration framework for complex, multi-step workflows involving reasoning, tool calls, evidence collection, repair proposals, approval, and verification.
The agent operates on top of the core engine. It must not replace deterministic analysis or become the only way to access product functionality.
Investigate findings across multiple files.
Trace cache-key dependencies and invalidation paths.
Gather additional evidence when necessary.
Consult Jev on bounded caching-strategy decisions.
Develop implementation and repair plans.
Propose source-code and Redis-configuration changes.
Request approval for consequential operations.
Apply approved changes in isolated environments.
Run relevant tests, linting, and static checks.
Benchmark changes where appropriate.
Report successful, unsuccessful, and inconclusive outcomes accurately.
Define explicit graph state, node responsibilities, routing decisions, stopping conditions, bounded retries, error handling, and verification stages.
Investigate checkpointing, resumability, human-in-the-loop approval, execution limits, and recovery from partial failures.
Do not use autonomous agents for operations that can be performed more reliably and cheaply through deterministic functions.
The agent must never silently apply high-risk changes or claim an optimization is correct without adequate evidence.
MCP Server and Developer Integrations
Provide an MCP integration that exposes EZ-Redis capabilities to compatible AI clients, including GitHub Copilot in VS Code.
Investigate the current MCP Python SDK, supported transports, authentication requirements, compatibility constraints, and the appropriate separation between MCP and internal application services.
analyze_caching analyze_project inspect_redis_usage recommend_caching_pattern inspect_runtime_metrics explain_finding plan_cache_optimization generate_patch validate_patch
The preceding tool names are candidates, not a finalized API.
Consolidate, rename, or separate tools based on real use cases, clear contracts, discoverability, and usability.
Define input schemas, output schemas, error behavior, permission requirements, execution limits, and expected side effects for every proposed tool.
MCP must remain a thin adapter over reusable application services. Business logic belongs in the core engine and application layer.
Determine whether FastAPI is needed alongside the MCP SDK.
If a separate HTTP API would provide meaningful value, define its responsibilities, authentication model, deployment requirements, and relationship with MCP.
Do not introduce FastAPI merely because it is familiar or because the application uses Python.
Do not assume MCP automatically intercepts every Redis-related conversation or every Redis query executed anywhere in a developer's system.
Investigate practical approaches for making EZ-Redis available when relevant: MCP tool discovery and invocation by compatible clients. Custom Copilot agent definitions and repository instructions. IDE-specific integrations where justified. Explicit CLI and API invocation. Client-library instrumentation and middleware. Query interception within supported, explicitly instrumented execution paths.
Explain the feasibility, limitations, maintenance costs, and security implications of each approach.
The product should assist developers when Redis-related work occurs without claiming universal interception or depending on behavior outside its control.
```

ez_redis_planning_prompt.production_readiness:
Treat security, reliability, performance, and operational safety as architectural requirements from the beginning.
```
Filesystem access boundaries and repository isolation. Untrusted repository content and prompt injection. Secret and credential handling. Redis authentication, TLS, and least-privilege access. Safe runtime inspection and diagnostic permissions. Command execution, process isolation, and sandboxing. Human approval for consequential operations. Timeouts, cancellation, resource limits, and bounded retries. Failure recovery and partial execution. LLM and Jev service outages and invalid responses. Observability and actionable diagnostics. Concurrency and state isolation between repositories. Large-repository performance and scalability. Incremental analysis and safe caching of analysis results. Deterministic outputs and reproducibility where required. API, MCP, and client compatibility. Dependency and software supply-chain security. Generated documentation versioning and migrations. Backward compatibility and upgrade strategy.
Treat source code, repository documents, external tool output, telemetry, and model-generated content as untrusted inputs.
Repository instructions and model output must never override system-level security policies.
Separate read-only analysis from operations that modify application source code, Redis data, infrastructure, or application behavior.
Design explicit permission boundaries, approval checks, auditability, and isolation appropriate to each operation.
```

ez_redis_planning_prompt.required_implementation_plan:
Produce a comprehensive plan in PLAN.MD. The plan must be specific enough to support implementation phase by phase without requiring a fresh architectural investigation for every phase.
```
Describe the recommended architecture, major components, product capabilities, and most consequential decisions.
Summarize verified repository state, existing functionality, architectural constraints, established conventions, and technical debt.
Include an architecture diagram and explain the responsibilities, interfaces, dependencies, and boundaries of the principal components.
Show the flow from source code and telemetry through the shared IR, findings, Jev, MCP, and LangGraph.
Identify deterministic components, probabilistic decision-making, optional capabilities, and external service dependencies.
Provide a justified dependency inventory, optional dependency groups, compatibility constraints, alternatives, packaging recommendations, and maintenance considerations.
Propose principal domain models, the shared IR, finding schema, Jev decision schema, MCP tool contracts, error models, and module boundaries.
Include illustrative schemas and pseudocode where useful, without implementing them.
Specify which Markdown files should be generated, when each is applicable, how content is derived and maintained, how stale documentation is detected, and how future analyses consume the documentation.
Divide implementation into small, ordered, independently testable phases.
Each phase must define: Objective. Scope and explicit non-goals. Expected files and modules affected. Dependencies and prerequisites. Technical approach. Tests and acceptance criteria. Risks and rollback strategy. Definition of done.
Prioritize a useful, reliable core before introducing expensive or high-complexity autonomous features.
Define datasets, fixtures, measurements, and quality gates for analyzer accuracy, recommendation quality, agent behavior, analysis performance, and target-application improvements.
Document permission boundaries, security controls, failure handling, isolation, observability, performance limits, and deployment considerations.
Identify high-risk assumptions, infeasible or misleading requirements, design alternatives, and decisions requiring developer input.
Recommend defaults when possible and distinguish known facts from unresolved uncertainty.
Provide an ordered checklist of proposed work, phase dependencies, acceptance criteria, and objective completion conditions.
```

quality_standards.principle: Prioritize correctness, developer trust, maintainability, and measurable usefulness over architectural complexity.
Do not assume deterministic analysis requires an LLM.
Do not assume Jev can infer complete application semantics from an entire repository without structured evidence.
Do not assume MCP guarantees automatic invocation whenever Redis is mentioned.
Do not claim universal Redis query interception without explicit instrumentation or control of the execution path.
Do not assume all caching problems can be solved by adding a TTL.
Do not recommend a caching pattern without evaluating workload, freshness, consistency, failure behavior, and operational cost.
Do not introduce a complex multi-agent system before establishing that simpler workflows are inadequate.
Do not introduce dependencies merely because they are popular or available.
Do not claim that benchmarks, tests, integrations, or specialist reviews were completed unless they actually were.
Distinguish verified facts, assumptions, proposals, inferences, and unresolved decisions throughout the report.
Challenge unnecessary, infeasible, overly expensive, redundant, or technically incorrect requirements.
